headerLink.description: One text link in the widget header's actions group, before the overflow menu (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): "All deadlines", "To the board". A `route` (named page, optional `params` / `query`) is a router link, an `href` a plain anchor. The label is an i18n key. Rendered by CnWidgetWrapper; CnDashboardPage reads it off the layout entry or the widget definition.

showButtons.description: `false` drops the widget's footer links (its definition's `buttons`, e.g. a calendar's "More events"), for a placement whose card says enough without them (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3).

sizeToContent.description: Opt-in: hand this placement's height to whatever it renders, so a widget that decides AT RUNTIME it has nothing to show costs no row. `true` sizes purely to content; an integer sizes to content too but caps the height at that many rows (GridStack's maximum, NOT a minimum: content shorter than N rows is as short as it is, content taller is clipped at N). It makes gridHeight advisory for this widget — right for anything whose height is whatever it turned out to be (a banner whose condition is false, a list that came back empty), wrong for anything with a deliberate size. Maps to CnDashboardGrid's per-item `sizeToContent`.

props.description: Optional widget-specific props passed at render time. Shape is widget-specific; not constrained here.

tabGroup.description: Optional: groups this widget into a named tab within the slot. Only meaningful for tab:* and section:* slots.

dataSource.description: Optional declarative data binding. Carry-forward from v1 widgetDef.dataSource — same shape.

dateChip.description: Opt-in (custom widgets only): when true AND the page's `dateRange.enabled` is true, the shared date-range chip renders in this widget's title bar (chart widgets with a `dataSource.bucket` get it automatically). Carry-forward from v1 layoutItem.dateChip — same semantics.

_note.description: Human-readable note. Optional on most widgets. REQUIRED when the containing page has type 'custom' — in that case this field must document why a standard page type was not feasible.

ncDashboard.description: Opt-in: also publish this placement as a widget on the native Nextcloud dashboard, alongside the app's own pages. An object rather than a boolean because a Nextcloud panel is a single narrow column with its own title, icon and link, none of which the grid placement carries. Presence of this key REQUIRES an `id` on the same entry (enforced in allOf below), and that id MUST be unique across the WHOLE manifest, not merely within its own page's widgets[] — Nextcloud's widget namespace is per app, so two pages both declaring id 'recent' derive one shared panel. Manifest-wide uniqueness is beyond JSON Schema; validateManifestV2 enforces it post-schema. Omitting the key leaves the widget visible only inside the app.

title.description: Panel title on the Nextcloud dashboard. Falls back to the widget's own title when omitted.

order.description: Initial ordering hint, passed through as IWidget::getOrder(). It decides where the panel first appears; once a user rearranges their own dashboard their arrangement wins, so this is a hint and never a guarantee.

link.description: In-app route the panel header links to, so a reader can open the page where the widget's full context lives. Written the way `pages[].route` is, e.g. '/reporting' — the host resolves it against its own app root with generateUrl() and never renders it bare. A scheme ('https:', and 'javascript:' above all) and a protocol-relative '//host' are both refused: the panel is rendered by Nextcloud's dashboard, outside this app's own pages, so a manifest is not a place to hand it an offsite destination.

allOf.description: ncDashboard requires a stable id. The host derives a permanent Nextcloud widget id from `id`, and Nextcloud stores each user's chosen widgets by that id in its own namespace, which no migration of this app can reach. A widget identified by array position would move onto a different widget whenever the array is reordered, silently changing what a user sees. `id`'s own pattern already refuses an empty string, so requiring the key is the whole of the rule expressible here; the manifest-wide uniqueness half lives in validateManifestV2.
sidebar slot: gridWidth MUST equal 1. The sidebar is a fixed-width panel; widgets always span the full width.
header-actions slot: gridY MUST equal 0. All header action widgets live in a single row.

object-table built-in widget: when props declares a `source` it must match the declarative self-fetch shape, an `endpointSource` (Wave 2) must match the shared endpoint binding (exactly one of source | endpointSource — post-schema check), and `actions` must be typed manifest actions (incl. type:'object-op'). Other props stay free-form (pass-through to CnDataTable).

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound rows — the payload at responsePath must be an array; columns / formatters / rowRoute / actions apply unchanged on top. Exactly one of source | endpointSource (post-schema check).

actions.description: Declarative row/widget actions rendered by CnWidgetObjectTable. object-op patch/delete render per row; object-op create renders as a widget-scoped footer affordance.

pageSize.description: Rows per page: the table shows one page with the board pager under it ("4 of 7", DqCatalogus). Under a pager `source.limit` is how many rows are read (2.127.0).

rowClass.description: #91: declarative per-row CSS class rules compiled into CnDataTable's rowClass function. Each rule { when: { field, op?, value }, class } adds `class` to a row when the shared visibleWhen predicate holds against that row (field = dot-path into the row, op = eq|neq|gt|gte|lt|lte default eq, value = literal). Rules evaluate in order and every matching class is space-joined — so overdue / at-risk rows can be highlighted from the manifest. A host-supplied rowClass FUNCTION (runtime-only) still passes straight through.

when.description: The predicate evaluated against the row (shared visibleWhen grammar, LOCAL form).

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

class.description: CSS class added to the row when `when` holds.

allOf.description: nav-card-grid built-in widget (ADR-044 §4 cards-collapse): props.entries is REQUIRED and each entry must match the navCardEntry shape. Unlike stats-block's optional entries[], nav-card-grid has no dataSource alternative — it renders arbitrary navigation links, not fetched data.

entries.description: One card per array entry, rendered by CnNavCardGrid.

allOf.description: stats-block built-in widget: when props declares `entries[]` each entry must match the statsBlockEntry shape. The exactly-one-of dataSource | props.entries constraint is a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (clear error message), not by JSON Schema.

entries.description: Multi-entry KPI sources — each entry renders one CnStatsBlock within the widget card. Mutually exclusive with a single dataSource.

allOf.description: banner built-in widget (CnBannerWidget, Wave 1): a declarative notice banner. props { variant, text, visibleWhen?, route? } — visibleWhen is a simple {endpoint|source, field?, op?, value} predicate evaluated at mount (fail-safe: hidden on fetch failure).

variant.description: Banner severity variant (NcNoteCard type). Default info.

text.description: Pre-translated banner text (required for the banner to render).

visibleWhen.description: Optional visibility condition: exactly one of `endpoint` (same-origin JSON URL) or `source` (OpenRegister object query). `field` is a dot-path into the response (source: into the first result; omit or use '@total' for the collection total). Fail-safe: the banner stays hidden until the predicate evaluates true.

source.description: OpenRegister object query; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

order.description: Order of the query (`{ field: "asc" | "desc" }`), so the first result is the first of an ordered list. With it an attention card names that row: `{subject.<field>}` in its title, reason and kicker and `@subject.<field>` in an action route read it (screens-start-here-banner, 2.89.0).

field.description: Dot-path into the response ('@total' or omitted = collection total for a source).

op.description: Comparison operator. `notEmpty` on `id` is the "there is a first row" test of a card that names one.

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

route.description: Optional click-through: a vue-router route NAME (string) or a full location object. Makes the banner text an accessible button.

layout.description: How the banner renders. `banner` (default) is the note card. `attention` is a card with a severity edge, a kicker, a title, a reason line and up to two actions.

stacked.description: Attention card: put the actions under the text instead of beside it, with a 16px title (PqMijnWerk "Begin hier"; screens-start-here-banner, 2.89.0).

kicker.description: Attention card: the small label above the title.

title.description: Attention card: the title. Falls back to `text`.

reason.description: Attention card: the line that says why this needs attention. `{value}` is replaced by the value visibleWhen read.

actions.description: Attention card: at most two actions. The first is the primary one unless an action sets `primary: true`.

id.description: Identifier passed with the `action` event of an action that has no route or href.

label.description: The text on the action.

route.description: A vue-router route NAME (string) or a full location object.

href.description: An URL, used when there is no route.

primary.description: Render this action as the primary one.

allOf.description: record-list built-in widget (CnRecordListWidget): the action under the list, `props.content.footerAction` (2.126.0), and a row's colour `dot` and `flags` (2.129.0). Other content keys stay free-form.

footerAction.description: One action under the list, also under the empty text (DqBezwaar "Beroep registreren"). Its other keys are an action's (`type`, `route`, `form`, ...). While `disabledWhen` holds it is disabled and says `disabledReason` ("Kan zodra de beslissing is verzonden"). Label and reason go through the host's translate.

dot.description: A colour dot before the title: a field name, or `{ field, colorMap? }` (2.129.0).

flags.description: The labels of the flags a row has, at its end ("Start", "End"): `[{ field, label, value? }]` (DqZaaktypeOverzicht, 2.129.0).

allOf.description: notice built-in widget (CnNoticeWidget): one toned box with an icon, a bold title and a text, through the host's translate, in the side column or the grid (DqSociaalDomein, 2.128.0).
related built-in widget (CnRelatedObjectsWidget): grouping by relation (2.129.0). Other content keys stay free-form.

groupByRelation.description: Split the Objects group by the relation label OpenRegister answers per direction.

layout.description: `sections` draws every group under its own heading in one list.

groupActions.description: An action on a group's heading in `layout: "sections"`, keyed by the group's key (DqZaakGerelateerd "Vervolg plannen").

allOf.description: nc-widget built-in widget (CnNcWidgetWidget): leaving items out (2.129.0). Other content keys stay free-form.

excludeApps.description: Apps whose items are left out (an item's app is its own app field, else the /apps/<app>/ part of its link or icon), e.g. ["systemtags"].

excludeTypes.description: Item types that are left out.

allOf.description: decision-list built-in widget (CnDecisionListWidget): per-row sign-offs, each with an answer, its fields and a reason, sent to an app endpoint (2.133.0). Texts go through the host translate.

title.description: A template filled from a row.

meta.description: A template filled from a row.

reason.description: `{ label?, required?, field? }` (required by default, sent as `field`, default `reason`); `false` drops it.

allOf.description: retention built-in widget (CnRetentionWidget): a record's stored retention, and a recompute for archivists (2.133.0). Texts go through the host translate.

archivistGroups.description: Groups that may recompute (default ["archivaris"]; admins always may).

allOf.description: plan built-in widget (CnPlanWidget): a record's planned steps from OpenRegister's case layer (2.133.0).
work-queue built-in widget (CnWorkQueue): one queue of everything waiting on the reader, in groups that can be hidden until tomorrow (2.133.0).

source.description: An endpointSource answering `{ groups, hiddenGroups?, unavailable? }`.

hide.description: A url template with `{group}` that hides a group until tomorrow.

show.description: A url template with `{group}` that shows a hidden group again.

itemHref.description: A template filled from an item, for items without `route` or `href`.

allOf.description: audit-trail built-in widget (CnAuditTrailWidget, Wave 1): the object change-log card. All props are optional — register/schema/objectId normally arrive via the detail-page object-context merge; explicit props win.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug/id (context merge fallback when omitted).

schema.description: OpenRegister schema slug (context merge fallback when omitted).

objectId.description: The audited object's id (context merge fallback when omitted).

allOf.description: chart widget display passthrough (Wave 1): additive presentation keys forwarded verbatim to CnChartWidget by CnDashboardPage's dispatcher and the v2 grid. Other chart props stay free-form.

legendPosition.description: Legend placement override (empty/omitted keeps the automatic placement).

valueAxisBaseline.description: Value-axis baseline: 'auto' (the default — zero for bar/area, a bounded window for line/scatter), 'zero' (force a zero baseline), or 'fit' (let ApexCharts frame the data range, for a series living far from zero such as an SLA hovering 95–99%).

valueFormat.description: Named value formatter applied to the value axis + tooltip: 'currency' | 'currency-compact' | 'percent' | 'number', or the object form { name, currency?, decimals?, suffix? }. 'number' with `suffix` reads '9 d'.

currency.description: ISO-4217 code (EUR default; invalid codes fall back to EUR).

suffix.description: Text after a 'number' value, e.g. ' d'.

colorMap.description: Per-category colour map ({ categoryLabel: cssColor }) for pie/donut/radialBar slices and (distributed) bar categories.

emptyLabel.description: Empty-state message rendered instead of the chart when the resolved series contain no data points.

barMax.description: chartKind 'bar-list': the value a full track stands for (100 for percentages). Omitted = the largest value.

footnote.description: A line under the chart, through the host's translate: under the rows of a bar-list or matrix, and under the plot of a line, area or bar chart.

referenceLines.description: line, area and bar charts: dashed horizontal reference lines on the value axis, such as a norm. Each `{ value, label?, color? }`; the label goes through the host's translate, the colour defaults to the theme's error colour.

categoryFormat.description: How date categories read on the x-axis: `month` ("jan") or `month-year` ("jan 2026"), in the user's language. Categories that are not dates are left as is.

emptyCellLabel.description: chartKind 'matrix': the text of a cell without a value ("geen"), through the host's translate. Empty leaves the cell blank. Passed through to CnChartWidget.

highlight.description: chartKind 'matrix': the cell to outline, usually the record's on a detail page. `row` matches a series key, name or 1-based position; `column` an entry of columnKeys, a category label or a 1-based position. Both take tokens such as '@object.behaviour'.

cellSource.description: chartKind 'matrix': read the cells from records that each hold one cell. The records are listed from register/schema with `filter` (tokens such as '@object.matrixVersion' resolved; the list waits while one is unresolved), then laid out by rowField / columnField with valueField as the cell. Labels come from rowLabels / columnLabels maps or rowLabelField / columnLabelField; order from rowOrder / columnOrder lists, else rowOrderField / columnOrderField, else natural order. valueLabels maps a stored value to the text shown; colorMap may key on either. With cellsPath the matrix sits inside ONE record: the first record filter finds (else fallbackFilter), its array at cellsPath narrowed by cellFilter (tokens allowed), and the axis order from rowOrderPath / columnOrderPath on that record. Wins over series / categories.

cellsPath.description: Path of the cells array inside the one record the source finds.

cellFilter.description: Equality filter on the cells of that record, e.g. { actorType: '@object.actorType' }.

fallbackFilter.description: Filter used when `filter` finds no record, e.g. { active: true }.

rowOrderPath.description: Path of an array on that record giving the row order.

columnOrderPath.description: Path of an array on that record giving the column order.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound series/labels — the shared endpoint transport plus the labelsPath / series[] {name, path} response mapping. Exactly one of dataSource | endpointSource (post-schema check).

allOf.description: tabs built-in widget (CnTabsWidget): `props.content.tabs[]` entries are a widget id or an object { id?, widgetId, label?, icon?, count?, countField?, unreadKey?, overflow?, visibleWhen? }. `visibleWhen` reuses the shared predicate: a tab whose condition is false is absent from the strip, not empty. LOCAL form reads a field of the page object; the `source` form counts related rows (`@total`) once on mount and after a reported write, and shows the tab disabled while it is pending. A tab without the key always renders.

header / text / divider on the v2 grid (Wave 1): the dashboard catalog's content-only presentation widgets reused as built-ins. Each takes a single `props.content` object with the same shape as its dashboard `content` blob.

content.description: The widget's content blob — header: { title, subtitle, backgroundImageUrl, overlayMode, height, cta, … }; text: { text, contentMode, fontSize, … }; divider: { style, lineColor, headingText, … }.

allOf.description: stat / delta catalog widgets on the v2 grid (Wave 2, #91): the KPI tiles take a `props.content` blob (same shape as their dashboard `content`). The endpoint-binding keys are typed here; the rest of the blob stays free-form (label, icon, format, source, …). Exactly one of content.source | content.endpointSource — a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (stats-block precedent), which also covers the legacy pages[].config.widgets[] placement.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound KPI value(s) — exactly one of source | endpointSource (post-schema check).

valueField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for the displayed (current) value. Omitted = the payload itself.

previousField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for the previous-period value — renders the trend sublabel (arrow + percent-vs-previous; the pipelinq previousPeriod contract).

deltaField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for a SERVER-computed delta percent — wins over the client-side previousField computation.

goodDirection.description: Which trend direction tints green ('up' default; 'down' for cost-like KPIs). The delta widget's source.goodDirection still wins for the OpenRegister form.

variantWhen.description: First-match threshold styling rules for the stat tile — the matched rule's variant re-tints the value + icon circle, and its optional icon overrides content.icon.

op.description: Comparison operator against the resolved display value (numeric when both sides coerce; eq/neq fall back to string equality).

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

variant.description: Colour variant applied on match ('default' keeps the configured colours). The component also accepts 'danger' as an alias of 'error' for doriath-migrated content.

icon.description: Optional MDI icon name overriding content.icon while this rule matches.

clickRoute.description: Whole-tile click-through: a vue-router route NAME (string) or full location object. Alias of content.route (route wins when both are set).

allOf.description: workspace-filter catalog widget (#91 Wave 3): a choice list whose selection writes into the page workspace context so sibling widgets refetch. The endpoint/OR-source binding keys of `props.content` are typed here; the rest stays free-form.

writes.description: The workspace context key the selection writes (`@workspace.<key>` or a bare `<key>`). Sibling widgets whose declarative source interpolates `@workspace.<key>` refetch on change.

style.description: Choice style: 'radio' (default) list, 'select' dropdown, 'chips' (one compact segmented group with a count after each label; screens-page-lenses, 2.87.0) or 'toggle' (a switch writing `onValue` / `offValue`; screens-page-controls, 2.88.0).

layout.description: 'start' draws the start card; 'bar' draws `controls` side by side in one row (screens-page-controls, 2.88.0).

controls.description: With `layout: "bar"`: the bar's controls, each a workspace-filter content (chips, a toggle, a select) with its own `writes`. `align: "end"` pushes a control to the right edge (2.88.0).

onValue.description: style 'toggle': the value written while the switch is on. Default true (2.88.0).

offValue.description: style 'toggle': the value written while the switch is off. Default false (2.88.0).

align.description: In a bar: 'end' pushes this control to the right edge (2.88.0).

urlKey.description: Keep the choice in the address as `?<urlKey>=<value>` (replacing the history entry, keeping other query keys). The address wins over `default` on load, so a chip is linkable (screens-page-lenses, 2.87.0).

allLabel.description: Optional leading 'All' option — writes the empty string so an optional sibling token (`@workspace.<key>?`) drops (unfiltered set).

options.description: Static options — each { value, label, count?, countFrom? } (or { id, name } / bare strings, normalised). `countFrom` is `{ register, schema, filter? }`, or a list of those that are added up; the option shows that list's total (one list request each; none when it fails). screens-page-lenses, 2.87.0.

source.description: OpenRegister /grouped facet source { register, schema, groupBy, filter? } — each distinct value becomes an option with its object count.

endpointSource.description: App endpoint returning an array of { value, label, count? } options at responsePath.

allOf.description: kb-search catalog widget (#91 Wave 3): summary-driven knowledge-base search through a PLUGGABLE PROVIDER. The provider seam keys of `props.content` are typed here; the rest stays free-form.

provider.description: Provider registry key (default 'default' — the built-in endpoint search). An app registers bespoke providers (the xwiki proxy) on CnAppRoot's kbSearchProviders; the xwiki client stays app-side.

space.description: Provider-specific KB space filter (passed to provider.search).

tags.description: Provider-specific tag filter — a single tag or an array.

endpoint.description: The default provider's search endpoint (OpenRegister xWiki leaf by default).

queryParam.description: The default provider's query parameter name (default 'q').

bindTo.description: Workspace context key to auto-search on (default 'activeSummary').

minChars.description: Minimum characters before a search fires (default 3).

limit.description: Result cap passed to the provider (default 8).

externalOpen.description: Whether result links open in a new tab (defaults to the provider's own externalOpen flag).

unavailableFallback.description: Text shown when the provider rejects / is unavailable (replaces the default 'Knowledge base unavailable').

allOf.description: week-strip catalog widget (CnWeekStripWidget): the current week as day columns with the dated items under each day. Takes a `props.content` blob. Items come from an OpenRegister `source` (one request for the week, bucketed by `dateField`) or from static `items`.

days.description: 5 working days (default) or the whole week. The week starts on Monday.

source.description: OpenRegister object query; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

limit.description: Cap on the records fetched for the week (default 100).

dateField.description: The field the items are bucketed by. Required with a source.

titleField.description: The field shown as the item title. Defaults to the object's display name.

itemRoute.description: Route name an item links to; the record id goes in params.id.

lateWhen.description: Rule on the number of days until the date that marks an item late. Default: before today ({ op: 'lt', value: 0 }).

lateField.description: A boolean field that marks a record late, whatever its date.

items.description: Static items, used when there is no source.

emptyText.description: Text of a day without items.

weekOffset.description: Whole weeks from the current one (1 = next week).

inset.description: Draw the strip inside the board's inset (16px above, 24px at the sides, 22px below) instead of from card edge to card edge (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Theme hook --cn-widget-board-inset.

allOf.description: stacked-bar catalog widget (CnStackedBarWidget): one segmented bar with a legend that carries the label and count of every segment. Takes a `props.content` blob. Segments come from one grouped count request (`source.groupBy`) or from static `segments`.

source.description: OpenRegister grouped count; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

groupBy.description: The field the records are counted per.

segments.description: Static segments, used when there is no source.

order.description: Group keys in the order they render. Unlisted groups follow; a listed key without records shows 0.

labels.description: The label of a group key.

inset.description: Draw the bar and legend inside the board's inset (16px above, 24px at the sides, 22px below) instead of from card edge to card edge (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Theme hook --cn-widget-board-inset.

fieldWidget.description: A declarative widget-component slot used inside `form` / `detail` page config. Distinct from the top-level pages[].widgets[] grid placement (which carries widgetKey + grid coordinates). fieldWidget mounts a lib `Cn*` SFC inline as a form field or detail data slot; the renderer resolves `component` against the lib's exported component map, NOT the host-app customComponents registry. Carries serialisable `props` only — handler / function props must be wired via the host App's manifest-level mounts. Replaces the untyped `fieldWidgets[]` key relied on by pipelinq#415 (which rode through on additionalProperties: true). See ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue#314.

id.description: Unique identifier within the fieldWidgets[] array. Lower-camel-case-ish: must start with a lowercase letter and contain only letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Used as the form field key / data binding key by CnFormPage / CnDetailPage.

component.description: Name of a lib component (e.g. CnMarkdownEditor, CnSchemaSelect). MUST be Cn-prefixed and resolved against the @conduction/nextcloud-vue exported component map. Host-app SFCs are not allowed here — those go through pages[].component on a type:'custom' page.

props.description: Serialisable props passed to the resolved component at render time. Shape is component-specific; not constrained here. Handler / function values are not supported through the manifest (the manifest is JSON).

_note.description: Optional human-readable note explaining the role of this declarative widget slot.

slotValue.description: Valid slot value. Either a literal slot name (body, sidebar, header-actions, footer, modal) or a tab:<id> / section:<id> pattern string.

oneOf.description: Named tab or section slot. Format: tab:<id> or section:<id> where <id> is at least one character.

dataSource.description: Declarative data binding for widgets. Forms: (a) shorthand {register, schema, filter?, aggregate: 'count'} — the lib builds a count query and resolves to {count}. (b) raw {graphql: {query, variables?, selectors}} — the lib issues the query and runs selectors. (c) #91 Wave 3 chart aggregation — `aggregate` as an OBJECT {groupBy, metric?: count|sum, sumField?, topN?, otherBucket?, labelResolve?} grouped over the schema's objects via OpenRegister's /grouped facet (client-side collection fallback), plus an optional sibling `drilldown` {route, filterParam}. Carry-forward from v1.3.0 widgetDef.dataSource.

filter.description: Shorthand: filter map inlined into the generated query.

aggregate.description: Shorthand aggregation. The STRING 'count' builds a GraphQL count query resolving to {count}. The OBJECT form (#91 Wave 3) is a chart-only categorical group-by served by OpenRegister's /grouped facet.

oneOf.description: #91 Wave 3 chart aggregation: group the schema's objects by `groupBy`, count (default) or sum `sumField`, keep the `topN` largest (sorted desc) and optionally fold the remainder into a translated 'Other' slice, resolving reference keys to labels/colours via `labelResolve`.

sumField.description: Numeric field summed when metric is 'sum' (required for sum).

topN.description: Keep the N largest groups (sorted by value desc).

otherBucket.description: Fold the post-topN remainder into a single translated 'Other' slice (sum of the rest). The Other bucket never drilldown-navigates.

labelResolve.description: Resolve reference (uuid) group keys to the referenced objects' display labels (and optional per-category colours) through the shared object store — the fkResolve pattern.

register.description: Register the reference points into (defaults to the dataSource register).

schema.description: Schema slug the reference points into.

labelField.description: Property used as the display label (default 'name').

colorField.description: Optional property read as a per-category CSS colour (feeds the chart's colorMap path).

drilldown.description: #91 Wave 3 (chart only): a segment/bar click navigates to `route` with the clicked category's RAW key in the query ({ [filterParam]: rawKey }). A `/`-prefixed route is a path, otherwise a route name. Works with the OBJECT `aggregate` and the legacy `groupBy` forms; the folded 'Other' bucket never navigates.

route.description: Destination route name, or a path when it starts with '/'.

filterParam.description: Query-param name the clicked category's raw key is written to.

selectors.description: Map of result-prop name to dot-path selector.

action.description: A page action: the fields of $defs/actionFields, nothing else, with children that are actions too. Row, bulk and navigation actions use it; header actions use $defs/headerAction.

actionFields.description: The fields of an action, shared by $defs/action and the non-link $defs/headerAction, which close it and constrain `children`. A typed page action with a discriminator field. The type field determines behaviour: handler (registry function), open-modal (modal by id), open-page (named route), navigate (URL), object-op (declarative OpenRegister mutation via useObjectStore), export (opens the shared CnMassExportDialog export launcher), open-form (schema-driven create dialog — CnActionButtons), refresh (bumps the cn:page:refresh signal), api-call (POST/PUT an app endpoint + toast + refresh — CnActionButtons/dispatchAction), agent (run a governed hermiq agent), run-node (invoke one OpenRegister flow node against the page object, config collected via a dialog sourced from the node's own declared form — CnActionButtons/dispatchAction, or-flow-run-node; distinct from the UNRELATED setup-wizard step type of a similar name, 'run-action'), toggle (two-way state button — CnActionButtons only, NOT dispatchable). When type is omitted, it defaults to 'handler' (back-compatibility with v1.3.0 action declarations). The Ajv instance is compiled with useDefaults: true so the default is applied during validation.

id.description: Unique action identifier within the page's actions array.

label.description: i18n key resolved by the consuming app's t() function at render time.

type.description: Action behaviour discriminator. Defaults to 'handler' when omitted (back-compat with v1.3.0). handler: calls a registry function; open-modal: opens a modal by target id; open-page: navigates to a named route; navigate: navigates to a URL; object-op: dispatches a declarative mutation (patch | delete | create) of an OpenRegister object via the shared object store; export: opens the shared CnMassExportDialog export launcher configured via entities[]/formats[] — the confirm payload ({format, entity?}) routes to the action's `handler` in the manifest actions map (the app's export service does the download). open-form (#91 Wave 3): CnActionButtons opens a schema-driven create dialog (CnAdvancedFormDialog) for the action's register/schema, saves + toasts + refreshes + optionally navigates to onSuccessRoute. refresh (#91 Wave 3): bumps the page-level cn:page:refresh event-bus signal so every endpoint-bound widget refetches. api-call (#91 Wave 3): POST/PUT the token-interpolated url with payload/params (JSON body, payload resolves @-tokens recursively at any depth) + success/error toast + auto page-refresh (unless refresh:false); confirm gating is surface-consumed intent (object-op precedent); download:true requests a binary blob and triggers a browser file download instead (auto-refresh defaults to OFF in that mode). agent (hermiq#41): run a governed hermiq agent against the page object — POSTs { register, schema, objectId, resultField?, skill?, prompt? } to /apps/hermiq/api/agents/{agent}/run-on-object (object-RBAC-scoped; dispatches the governed AgentRunRequestedEvent). register/schema/objectId default to the page's @register/@schema/@objectId object context. A first-class companion to api-call (which remains the fallback for a bespoke body); hermiq is NOT hard-required — an app-level 404 surfaces a graceful 'agent runtime unavailable' toast. toggle (#91 Wave 3): a stateful two-way state button rendered by CnActionButtons (GET stateSource on mount, optimistic write on click) — NOT dispatchable through dispatchAction. object-op declares mutation INTENT only — authority is enforced server-side by OpenRegister RBAC (ADR-022/ADR-023); authorization-shaped fields have no client-side effect and are not accepted here.

op.description: object-op only: the mutation verb. patch merges `values` into the row's object (row-scoped); delete removes the row's object (row-scoped, ALWAYS confirm-gated); create adds a new object built from `values` against the widget's source register/schema (widget-scoped footer/header affordance). Required when type is 'object-op'.

values.description: object-op only: the verb's payload. For patch: the partial object merged over the row's object. For create: the new object's properties. Omitted for delete.

confirm.description: Confirm-gating (object-op + #91 Wave 3 api-call / open-form + agent): when true, the action presents a CnConfirmDialog before running (the dispatcher / CnActionButtons runs AFTER confirmation). object-op delete ALWAYS confirms regardless of this flag.

target.description: Destination for open-modal (modal id), open-page (route name), or navigate (URL). Ignored for handler type.

props.description: Additional props forwarded to the handler or modal.

createOverride.description: Registry handler name that owns the persist for an `open-form` action, replacing the default objectStore.saveObject. Resolved exactly as CnIndexPage resolves its own `createOverride` prop (a kind:'create-override' entry's `.handler`, a function-valued registry entry, or a function in the legacy customComponents map). Needed when the schema requires a field the create form cannot supply on its own — a server-minted foreign key, say — where a straight save would 400.

includeFields.description: open-form: the only fields the create dialog asks for. One schema often backs two surfaces, a detail page that edits all of it and a header button that collects what someone filing a new one types, and this is how the button says which it is. Omit for the whole schema.

excludeFields.description: open-form: fields the create dialog leaves out. Use it to drop a handful; use includeFields when it is easier to name what stays.

fieldOverrides.description: open-form: per-field overrides passed to fieldsFromSchema, keyed by field. Recognised keys include label, order, hidden, readOnly and widget.

advanced.description: open-form: open the properties-and-JSON table (CnAdvancedFormDialog) instead of the plain form. The plain form is the default because a header button is aimed at someone filing a record, not at inspecting its schema.

formTitle.description: open-form: overrides the create dialog's heading. Defaults to 'Create {schema title}'.

formEyebrow.description: open-form: the context line above the create dialog's heading (board look), e.g. the list the record joins. Through the host translate. Absent: no line.

formSubtitle.description: open-form: the sentence under the create dialog's heading (board look), e.g. which fields are required and what happens on save. Through the host translate. Absent: no sentence.

size.description: open-form: how wide the create dialog is, passed straight to NcDialog. Widen a form that asks enough questions to need scrolling; pair it with columns: 2.

columns.description: open-form: how many columns the fields flow into. 2 pairs them up, which halves the scrolling on a longer form. Textareas and JSON editors still span the full width, and the layout collapses to one column below 700px. Widen the dialog with size: 'large' as well, or two columns are merely two narrow ones.

endpoint.description: open-form only: edit a record that is not a register object through an endpoint (an OpenRegister organisation). `url` is where the save goes (token-interpolated, app-relative or absolute), `method` is PATCH (default) or PUT, or POST to create a record with an empty form, `loadUrl` reads the record when it differs from `url`, `responsePath` plucks it from the answer. The fields are `formProperties`. Without `endpoint` the action is the schema-driven create form.

formProperties.description: open-form with `endpoint` only: the fields the form shows and sends, as JSON-schema properties (`{ "name": { "type": "string", "title": "Name" } }`).

handler.description: Registry key for type: 'handler'. Resolved across both registries passed to CnAppRoot: a v2 `registry` entry of `kind: 'handler'` exposing the function as `.handler` (or `.fn`), a directly function-valued registry entry, or a function-valued entry in the deprecated `customComponents` map. The same resolution serves actions[], bulkActions[] and headerActions[]. Also the built-in dispatch verb when paired with `route` (handler: 'navigate' → $router.push to `route`).

route.description: Destination route name for handler: 'navigate'. The dispatcher (manifestActionDispatch) calls $router.push({ name: route, params }). For row-level actions params include { id: row[rowKey] } automatically — do NOT restate it as params: { id: "{id}" }, though that placeholder does resolve (see `params`). Page-level header actions navigate without row context (e.g. a 'New X' action to a detail route).

icon.description: Optional icon for the action, rendered by CnActionsBar. Either an MDI icon name (e.g. 'TextBoxOutline') or a CSS icon class (e.g. 'icon-file').

entities.description: export only: selectable entity types offered by the export launcher (e.g. Leads / Requests). Optional — when absent the dialog shows only the format picker. Each entry needs an id + pre-translated label.

id.description: Entity id handed to the confirm handler.

label.description: Pre-translated display label.

formats.description: export only: the offered export formats — bare ids ('excel', 'csv', 'json' — lifted to {id, label} with an upper-cased label) or full {id, label} entries. Optional — the dialog's built-in Excel/CSV defaults apply when absent.

id.description: Format id handed to the confirm handler.

label.description: Pre-translated display label.

description.description: export only: pre-translated description shown above the export launcher's pickers.

url.description: api-call / toggle only: the app endpoint (POST/PUT). App-relative (routed through generateUrl) or absolute (http/https). May interpolate @objectId / @object.<field> / @workspace.<key> / @config.<key> tokens inline, as well as the literal {objectId} brace placeholder (unresolved tokens collapse to empty).

method.description: api-call: HTTP method (default POST); GET sends the resolved params as the query string, and with download: true downloads the file the endpoint answers (DqDoorlooptijd). toggle writeUrl: default PUT.

payload.description: api-call only: the JSON request body — PREFERRED over `params`, and used instead of it when both are set. Values run the SAME token grammar as `params` (@me, @now, @today±Nd, @monthStart/@quarterStart/@yearStart, @objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` marking a value OPTIONAL — dropped when unresolved) but resolve RECURSIVELY at ANY nesting depth, including arrays of objects — e.g. a Filinq document-generation body: { "dataRefs": [{ "register": "crm", "schema": "lead", "id": "@objectId" }] }. A required (non-`?`) token left unresolved anywhere in the tree BLOCKS the call (error toast) instead of sending the literal token string to the server.

params.description: Two distinct uses depending on the action's dispatch. (1) api-call / toggle: the JSON request body (legacy — prefer `payload` for anything with nested objects/arrays; ignored when `payload` is set). Values run the shared filter-token grammar ONE level deep (@me, @today±Nd, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values dropped when unresolved; a required unresolved token skips the call). (2) handler: 'navigate' (index-page row actions, manifestActionDispatch): vue-router params merged OVER the default { id: row[rowKey] }. OMIT it for the ordinary 'open this row's detail page' action — the row id is already injected. String values run the `{field}` ROW-token grammar (NOT the @-token grammar): "{id}" resolves to row.id with its type preserved, "run-{id}" interpolates as text, and a brace-less "new" stays literal (that is what makes a 'New X' action navigate with { id: 'new' }). A token naming a field the row does not carry is dropped with a console.warn — so `id` falls back to the row id — instead of being pushed as a literal %7Bid%7D path segment.

download.description: api-call only: request the response as a binary blob (axios responseType 'blob') and trigger a browser file download instead of a JSON toast+refresh cycle. The filename is taken from the response's Content-Disposition header, else the token-resolved `filename`, else 'download.pdf'. The success toast still shows; unlike a normal api-call the page does NOT auto-refresh afterwards unless `refresh: true` is explicitly set.

filename.description: api-call `download: true` only: fallback filename used when the response carries no Content-Disposition header (falls back further to 'download.pdf'). Interpolates the same token grammar as `url` (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>, {objectId}).

successMessage.description: api-call / open-form / agent / run-node / toggle: pre-translated success toast text (a library default applies when absent; agent default 'Run queued').

errorMessage.description: api-call / agent / run-node / toggle: pre-translated error toast text (falls back to the server's error/message, then a library default; an agent 404 with no structured body toasts 'agent runtime unavailable' instead).

refresh.description: api-call / agent / run-node / toggle: bump the page-level cn:page:refresh signal after a successful call (default true; set false to skip). EXCEPTION: for an api-call with download:true the default flips to false — a file download normally shouldn't also force-refetch every widget — set refresh:true explicitly to opt back in.

flowId.description: run-node only (REQUIRED): the published flow's uuid whose node this action invokes. A node's config and eligibility are properties of the flow it lives in (RN-3, OpenRegister's or-flow-run-node), so the manifest names which flow's instance to call rather than a bare node type — two flows could each carry the same node TYPE wired differently.

nodeId.description: run-node only (REQUIRED): the id of the node, within flowId's published graph, to invoke directly. POSTed to /api/flows/{flowId}/nodes/{nodeId}/run — refused (404) unless that node type has opted in to direct invocation (IFlowDirectlyInvokable).

subject.description: run-node only: the subject object the node acts on and is authorized against (OpenRegister object-RBAC — the caller needs update permission on it; the flow's own flow.run right is deliberately NOT what gates this). Typically @objectId; may interpolate the shared @-token grammar. An unresolved required token BLOCKS the call, matching agent's objectId.

agent.description: agent only (REQUIRED): the hermiq agent uuid to run against the page object. POSTed to /apps/hermiq/api/agents/{agent}/run-on-object (hermiq#41) — object-RBAC-scoped, dispatches the governed AgentRunRequestedEvent. May interpolate the shared @-token grammar (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>).

skill.description: agent only: optional skill id folded into the governed run (interpolates the same @-token grammar as `agent`).

prompt.description: agent only: optional prompt handed to the governed run. Interpolates the shared @-token grammar inline (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>) so it can be grounded on the page object — e.g. 'Summarise @object.title'.

resultField.description: agent only: the object field the agent's result is written back to (falls back to hermiq's default result field when absent).

objectId.description: agent only: the target object id. Defaults to the page object context's @objectId; an unresolved required @objectId BLOCKS the call (fail-closed) rather than sending a literal token. May be an explicit id or an @-token string.

register.description: open-form / agent / run-node: OpenRegister register slug. open-form: the create dialog's schema register. agent / run-node: the register the subject object belongs to — falls back to the page object context's @register.

schema.description: open-form / agent / run-node: OpenRegister schema slug. open-form: the create dialog fetches this schema and saves the new object against it. agent / run-node: the schema the subject object belongs to — falls back to the page object context's @schema.

onSuccessRoute.description: open-form only: optional post-save navigation target (#91). A bare route NAME (string) navigates with the saved object's id merged into the route params under `id` (harmless when the route has no `:id` segment — backward compatible). The object form { name, paramField?, objectParam? } names the id param (`paramField`, default `id`) and, when `objectParam` is set, also passes the whole saved object under that param key (for a props:true detail route to render without a refetch). The id is read from saved.id, then saved.uuid, then saved['@self'].id.

name.description: The vue-router route NAME pushed after a successful save.

paramField.description: Route param name populated from the saved object's id (default `id`).

objectParam.description: When set, the whole saved object is passed under this route param (props:true detail routes render without a refetch).

labelOn.description: toggle only: button label rendered while the state is ON (true). Falls back to `label`.

labelOff.description: toggle only: button label rendered while the state is OFF (false). Falls back to `label`.

stateSource.description: toggle only: the endpoint the initial state is read from on mount (the shared endpointSource shape — url + token-resolved params + responsePath). The `field` dot-path picks the boolean off the payload.

writeUrl.description: toggle only: the endpoint the flipped state is written to on click (interpolates the same tokens as `url`).

field.description: toggle only: the state field — read off the stateSource payload on mount AND sent (as the flipped boolean) in the write body under this key.

variant.description: CnActionButtons button variant (e.g. 'primary', 'secondary', 'error'). 'error' also styles the confirm dialog as destructive. A 'primary' action is never collapsed into CnActionButtons' overflow menu and consumes none of its `inline` slots: NcActions paints all of its inline actions with one shared variant, so a lone primary among them is not expressible.

children.description: Sub-actions, rendered by CnActionButtons as this action's OWN chevron dropdown beside its button — deliberately not folded into the page's single overflow menu, because NcActions cannot nest and a list that grows per record (app versions, say) would swamp it. Children take the same shape as any action, `visibleWhen` included, and an action carrying them consumes none of the `inline` slots. The parent itself still renders its own button beside the chevron (`type` defaults to 'handler' when omitted), so a parent meant only to group its children needs a `handler` that does something meaningful — an untyped, handler-less parent renders a button that dispatches to nothing. Each child is an action; a header action's child is a header action, so it may be a link with `href`.

childrenLabel.description: i18n key naming the `children` dropdown. Falls back to the parent action's own label, so the chevron is never announced unlabelled.

group.description: Detail page header actions only. i18n key / text naming the group this action sits in inside the overflow menu. Grouped actions render under a caption with this name, in first appearance order, after the ungrouped ones. Ignored on other surfaces.

adminOnly.description: Detail page header actions only. Shows the action to instance admins alone, in the last group of the overflow menu. Hides a control and nothing more: the endpoint behind the action still decides who may call it. Ignored on other surfaces.

visibleWhen.description: #91 Wave 3: an optional predicate gating whether the action renders — the shared banner shape ({ endpoint | source | field, op, value }). The `field`-only LOCAL form evaluates against the page object context (a detail action shown only in the right lifecycle state); endpoint / source forms fetch. Fail-safe: a broken predicate hides the action.

allOf.description: object-op actions MUST declare their mutation verb via `op`.
api-call actions MUST declare their endpoint via `url`.
open-form actions MUST declare the create schema via `schema`.
agent actions MUST declare the target agent uuid via `agent`.
toggle actions MUST declare their write endpoint via `writeUrl`.
run-node actions MUST declare which flow and which node within it (RN-3, or-flow-run-node) — a node's config and eligibility are properties of the flow it lives in, so neither can be inferred.

headerAction.description: A page header action (`headerActions[]`, a detail page's `quickActions[]` / `primaryActionByStage` entry, and their `children[]`): an action ($ref action), or with `href` a link ($ref headerLinkAction). Only header actions take `href`; row, bulk and navigation actions do not (2.135.0).

headerLinkAction.description: A header action that is a real link (`<a href>`), so it can be middle-clicked, opened in a new tab, copied and bookmarked. It only navigates: it runs no handler and emits no `header-action`, so it carries no `handler` and no other `type` (2.135.0).

id.description: Unique action identifier within the page's actions array.

label.description: i18n key resolved by the consuming app's t() function at render time.

href.description: The link. An absolute `http(s)`, `mailto:` or `tel:` URL and a protocol-relative `//host/...` URL are used as written. A path starting with a Nextcloud entry point (`/index.php/`, `/remote.php/`, `/public.php/`, `/ocs/`) is prefixed with the instance root unless it already starts with it; any other instance path (leading `/`, e.g. `/apps/integriq/connections`) goes through `generateUrl()`.

target.description: `_blank` opens the link in a new tab; `_self` opens it in place.

type.description: Only the default; a link has no other behaviour.

icon.description: Optional icon: an MDI icon name or a CSS icon class, as on any action.

variant.description: CnActionButtons button variant, as on any action.

group.description: Detail page header actions only: the overflow menu group, as on any action.

adminOnly.description: Detail page header actions only: show the link to instance admins alone, as on any action.

visibleWhen.description: An optional predicate gating whether the link renders, as on any action.

children.description: Sub-actions in the link's own chevron dropdown, as on any action.

childrenLabel.description: Name of the sub-action chevron, as on any action.

fieldValidation.description: manifest-form-logic: per-field validation rules for `type: 'form'` pages, enforced client-side by CnFormPage's validateFieldValue() before dispatch. Per-type semantics: string/password — required = non-empty after trim, min/max = string LENGTH, pattern tested against the value; number — required = finite number, min/max = numeric VALUE, pattern not applicable; boolean — required = value must be true (consent checkboxes), min/max/pattern not applicable; enum — required = a value is selected, min/max/pattern not applicable; json — required = non-null, min/max/pattern not applicable. Type-inapplicable rules are rejected by validateManifestV2() post-schema (pattern only on string/password; min/max only on string/password/number). `message` (i18n-able) overrides the built-in default message for whichever rule fails.

required.description: Whether the field must be filled. Default false. Per-type pass condition — see the fieldValidation description.

min.description: Minimum bound. String length for string/password fields, numeric value for number fields. MUST be <= max when both are set (validateManifestV2 post-schema check).

max.description: Maximum bound. String length for string/password fields, numeric value for number fields.

pattern.description: ECMAScript regex source tested against string/password values (implicit full-value test via new RegExp(pattern).test(value)). MUST compile — validateManifestV2() post-schema check runs `new RegExp(pattern)` in a try/catch.

message.description: i18n-able override message shown for ANY failing rule on this field, in place of the built-in translated default. Run through the page's `translate` prop, like `field.label`.

visibleWhen.description: #91 Wave 3: the shared visibility predicate (the Wave-1 banner shape). THREE modes: `endpoint` (GET a JSON endpoint, `field` dot-paths into the body), `source` (an OpenRegister { register, schema, filter? } query — `field` into the first result, or omit / use @total for the collection total), or LOCAL (neither endpoint nor source — `field` dot-paths into the caller's object context, e.g. a detail-page record). `op` defaults to eq. Evaluation is FAIL-SAFE (any error → hidden).

appInstalled.description: Nextcloud app id that must be installed and enabled for the guarded element to show. A PRECONDITION rather than a fourth mode: it is checked before anything else, and on its own it is the whole condition. Combined with endpoint/source/field it gates that mode too, so both must hold. It exists because the menu's `visibleIf` already spoke this word and `visibleWhen` did not, so the same manifest vocabulary meant two different things in two places. Use it on an action that writes into a sibling app, so an install without that app shows no button rather than a form that saves nowhere.

endpoint.description: A same-origin URL returning JSON; `field` is a dot-path into the body.

source.description: An OpenRegister object query { register, schema, filter? } (filter supports the shared @-token grammar). `field` dot-paths into the first result; omit it (or use @total) to compare the collection total.

workspace.description: WORKSPACE mode (screens-page-lenses, 2.87.0): the key of the page workspace context to compare, read at once with no request. A page control (a `workspace-filter` with `writes`) sets the key, and a dashboard widget carrying this condition appears and disappears as it changes. Honoured on a dashboard widget or KPI-row tile only, and as a top-level condition (not inside `all` / `any`).

field.description: Dot-path to the compared value — into the endpoint body, the source's first result, or (LOCAL mode) the caller's object context.

op.description: Comparison operator (default eq). eq/neq compare loosely-normalised primitives; ordering operators coerce both sides to Number. `in` holds when the value is one of the listed `value` array (2.87.0). `anyOf` holds when the value, or any entry of a list value, is one of the listed `value` array: a record whose `dataCategories` holds "health" among others matches `anyOf ["health", "ethnicity"]` (2.126.0). `contains` holds when a list value holds the given `value`, e.g. a case type's overviewCards switching a card on (2.128.0). `empty` / `notEmpty` take no `value` and treat undefined, null, '' and an empty array alike — the one question eq cannot ask, because an unset field arrives in a shape that depends on the store and String(null) is the word 'null' rather than blank.

value.description: The right-hand side of the comparison, resolved through the shared @-token grammar so `@me` names the signed-in reader rather than a literal only the server knows. Omitted for `empty` / `notEmpty`.

all.description: Every listed condition must hold. Use it where a gate is more than one fact — a Claim button that is both 'not closed' and 'nobody holds it'. Each entry is a full visibleWhen and may compose again.

any.description: At least one listed condition must hold. Ignored when `all` is also present.

objectTableSource.description: Declarative self-fetch source for the object-table built-in widget (CnWidgetObjectTable). The widget resolves `filter` @-tokens (@me, @today, @today±Nd, @workspace.*, ?-optional suffix) with the shared resolveFilterTokens grammar just before fetching, and drives CnDataTable's existing self-fetch. `register` MAY carry an `@resolve:` sentinel — the widget passes it through unexpanded (resolution is the host loader's responsibility). Externally supplied `rows` always win over `source`.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug (or an `@resolve:<key>` sentinel, passed through unexpanded by the widget).

filter.description: Filter map (`{ field: value | value[] | { op: value | value[] } }`). Values may use the shared @-token grammar: `@me` (current user via @nextcloud/auth), `@now`, `@today`, relative-date arithmetic `@today±Nd` at day granularity (e.g. `@today-30d`, `@today+7d`), `@monthStart`/`@quarterStart`/`@yearStart`, `@objectId`/`@object.<field>` (detail context), `@workspace.<key>`/`@config.<key>` with a trailing `?` for optional clauses that drop when unresolved. IN-lists: an ARRAY value (directly, or via `{ in: [...] }`) matches any of its entries — tokens resolve item-by-item and the widget serializes the list as repeated `field[]` params (the shape OpenRegister parses).

order.description: Fetch ordering: field name to direction map (e.g. { "dueDate": "asc" }).

limit.description: Row cap. 0 (or omitted) shows all fetched rows; a positive value caps the rendered rows and enables the View-all footer when more rows exist.

extend.description: OpenRegister `_extend[]` values forwarded on the fetch (e.g. ["calculations"]) so read-time virtual/derived fields are hydrated and available as columns. Each entry is passed through verbatim.

pageControls.description: screens-page-controls (2.88.0): which page controls a list widget (`record-list`, `object-table`) listens to, and what they mean for it. A page control is a `workspace-filter` select or switch that writes a workspace key. `sort` picks the list's sort from the key's value; `toggle` drops filter keys while the key is on. Without it the list ignores the page's controls.

sort.description: The workspace key a sort select writes, and what each of its values sorts by. A value with no entry leaves the list's own sort.

toggle.description: The workspace key a switch writes. While it is on (true, 1, "1", "true") the filter keys in `removes` are dropped, so a list that hides finished work shows it.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): ONE coherent endpoint data binding shared by the stat / delta / object-table widgets (the chart uses the extended $defs/chartEndpointSource). Reads an arbitrary app REST endpoint through the library's useEndpointSource engine: params pass the SAME @-token grammar widget filters use (@me, @today±Nd, @monthStart, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values that drop when unresolved — a REQUIRED token that stays unresolved blocks the fetch), requests dedupe + short-TTL cache per (method, url, resolved params), and the widget refetches on cn:page:refresh / a matching cn:widget:refresh. Exactly ONE of the widget's OpenRegister source | endpointSource may be configured — a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (clear error message), matching the stats-block precedent.

url.description: Endpoint URL — app-relative (routed through generateUrl, e.g. '/apps/pipelinq/api/analytics/overview') or absolute (http/https, left untouched). May interpolate @page.<key> / @workspace.<key> / @config.<key> / @objectId / @object.<field> tokens inline; unresolved URL tokens collapse to an empty string.

method.description: HTTP method. GET (default) sends the resolved params as query parameters; POST sends them as the JSON body.

params.description: Request parameters. Values pass the shared filter-token grammar (resolveFilterTokens): @me, @now, @today, @today±Nd, @monthStart/@quarterStart/@yearStart, @objectId/@object.<field> (detail context), @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values (dropped when unresolved; e.g. `{ "period": "@workspace.datePreset?" }` rides the dashboard date-range pills). A required token that stays unresolved blocks the fetch until the page context provides it.

responsePath.description: Dot-path pluck of the response payload (e.g. 'summary', 'data.series'). Omitted = the whole response body.

chartEndpointSource.description: The chart widget's endpoint binding: the $defs/endpointSource transport plus the labels/series response mapping. The mapping keys live INSIDE this block (not as sibling props) because the chart's flat `series` / `labels` props already carry the static data. When the plucked payload is an ARRAY of points (e.g. pipelinq /api/analytics/trends → responsePath 'series'), labelsPath / series[].path are PER-ITEM field paths (labelsPath 'date', series [{ name: 'Leads', path: 'value' }]); when it is an OBJECT they point at parallel arrays. Pie-family charts flatten the FIRST mapped series into the flat value array ApexCharts expects. Exactly ONE of dataSource | endpointSource per chart widget (post-schema check).

url.description: Endpoint URL — app-relative (generateUrl) or absolute. Same token interpolation as $defs/endpointSource.

method.description: HTTP method. GET (default) sends params as query parameters; POST as the JSON body.

params.description: Request parameters — the shared filter-token grammar (see $defs/endpointSource.params). Params re-resolve and the chart refetches when the dashboard date range changes (the page publishes dateFrom / dateTo / datePreset into the workspace context).

responsePath.description: Dot-path pluck of the response payload. Omitted = the whole response body.

labelsPath.description: Labels/categories mapping: a per-item field path for an ARRAY payload ('date'), or the path of a parallel label array for an OBJECT payload ('labels').

rowsPath.description: Path of an array of rows, one series each (chartKind 'matrix': one row per case type). Each row's name is at rowLabelPath and its values at rowValuesPath; the columns are at labelsPath.

rowLabelPath.description: Per-row path of the series name (default 'label').

rowValuesPath.description: Per-row path of the values array (default 'values').

series.description: Series mapping — one entry per rendered series.

name.description: Series display name (legend / tooltip). Defaults to the path.

path.description: Value mapping: a per-item field path for an ARRAY payload ('value'), or the path of a parallel number array for an OBJECT payload ('totals').

statsBlockEntry.description: One KPI entry inside a multi-entry stats-block widget (CnStatsBlockWidget `entries[]`). Carries the same source contract as a type:'stat' widget: register + schema + metric + token-resolved filter (@today / @me / @workspace.* and ?-optional clauses), plus per-entry presentation (title, variant, countLabel, format), an optional route deep link, and hideWhenZero. A money value names its currency with currencyField (the page object's field) or currency.

title.description: KPI title rendered by the inner CnStatsBlock.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug for this entry's count.

schema.description: OpenRegister schema slug for this entry's count.

metric.description: Aggregation metric for the REST /value aggregation (default 'count').

field.description: Field the metric aggregates over (metric-dependent; unused for count).

filter.description: Filter map with the shared @-token grammar (@today / @me / @workspace.<key>, trailing `?` for optional clauses).

route.description: Optional vue-router location for the KPI's deep link (renders the entry clickable).

variant.description: Color variant forwarded to the inner CnStatsBlock.

countLabel.description: Label displayed next to the count.

iconClass.description: Optional Nextcloud core icon class (icon-link, icon-mail, …) for the entry.

hideWhenZero.description: When true, the entry is omitted from the card when its resolved count is 0.

format.description: How the value is shown, as a type:'stat' widget's content.format: a style name, or { style, currency, currencyField, decimals, prefix, suffix }. Omitted, the plain localized count is shown. Numbers are formatted with Intl in the user's locale.

currency.description: ISO-4217 code, or a token such as @config.currency or @object.currency.

currencyField.description: Field of the detail page's object that holds the currency (dot-path allowed).

currency.description: Shorthand for format.currency: an ISO-4217 code, or a token such as @config.currency. Implies format 'currency'.

currencyField.description: Shorthand for format.currencyField: the field of the detail page's object that holds the currency, e.g. 'currency'. Implies format 'currency'. The currency is taken from the object, then currency, then the app's reporting currency (config currency), then EUR.

calendarView.description: The calendar view of this list: the current filtered rows on a month by a date field (config.calendar). Index pages only, and only offered when config.viewModes also lists `calendar`. Only the visible month is fetched. It reads and reschedules nothing: dragging an entry to another day is not offered.

dateField.description: The date property a row is placed on.

endDateField.description: Optional end date; a row then spans every day from dateField to endDateField.

titleField.description: The property shown on the entry; falls back to title, name or the row key.

formSmartPaste.description: Fill from pasted text on a form page (form-smart-paste). `fields` lists the config.fields[] keys the fill may write; `handler` names a customComponents entry (a function, or { fill, available }) that proposes the values; `hint` is shown above the paste box. Never offered on a public form. Cross-field rules (each field key is declared, handler present when enabled, mode not public) are checked by validateManifestV2().

formFieldLiveValues.description: form-live-values: the live-value keys a form field may carry on top of its type, label and key. `assign` is a list of { when, value } rules: the first whose visibleWhen-style `when` holds sets the field when an answer it reads changes (value: a literal, @answer.<field> or a sentinel token); once the user edits the field by hand its rules stop. `default` may be a sentinel token (@me, @me.displayName, @me.email, @today, @now, @object.<field>) resolved once when the form opens; an initial value wins. `calculate.inputs` names the answers a host `calculate` function reads for this read-only field. Other field keys are unchanged.

copySettings.description: index-copy-with-relations: what a copy on this index page may take along. `include` lists the link kinds: relationRows (the source's relation rows are re-created on the copy), incoming (the copy is added next to the source in every array-valued reference that points at it; a single-valued reference is never moved) and files (the attached files). The copy dialogs list the included kinds, ticked, and the copy is one request to OpenRegister's copy endpoint. Without `include` a copy carries the fields only.

page.description: A v2 page definition. CnPageRenderer dispatches by type and matches by $route.name === page.id. All page types support a uniform widgets[] array for declarative slot placement. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed in id, route, component, headerComponent, actionsComponent, or slots.* — those are router and registry invariants.

requiresApp.description: Soft dependency gating this WHOLE page. When the named Nextcloud app is not installed, the page renders the missing-dependency screen instead of its body. This is for the DEEP LINK: an entry gated by visibleIf.appInstalled is already hidden from the menu, so the remaining ways in are a bookmark, a shared URL, a redirect or an e2e spec, and those otherwise land on an empty page where 'not installed' looks the same as 'no data'. Gate a single WIDGET with visibleIf.appInstalled instead: a detail page may carry many widgets where only one needs the app, and that widget should hide while the page renders normally.

name.description: Human-readable app name shown on the screen; defaults to the id.

id.description: Vue-router route name. MUST be unique across pages[]. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

route.description: Path pattern (e.g. '/decisions', '/decisions/:id'). Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

type.description: Page type. Closed enum of 18 supported types. 'links' mounts CnLinkCardsPage: a page of link cards grouped under captions, declared with config.categories + config.cards ($defs/linkCard). Use it for the pages a short menu leaves out; unlike 'reports' an app may have several. 'flow' opens ONE flow in the editor; the flow LIST is an ordinary 'index' with config.entitySource='flows'. 'flows' and 'flow-detail' are DEPRECATED aliases kept for migration — 'flows' predates named index sources and 'flow-detail' is the old name for 'flow'. 'roadmap' mounts CnFeaturesAndRoadmapPage (features + GitHub-issue-backed roadmap). 'search' mounts CnSearchPage (cross-schema query + facet sidebar + results list; consumers wire the actual search via @search). 'wiki' mounts CnWikiPage (manifest-declared markdown article + optional sidebar tree; MUST declare config.register + config.schema). 'flow' and the deprecated 'flow-detail' both mount CnFlowEditorPage (the shared node/edge canvas) and take config.app to scope to the owning app. A flow lives in OpenRegister's native flow store rather than a register/schema pair, so a single flow cannot be a 'detail' page — but the LIST is a plain 'index' once a named entitySource supplies it, which is why 'flows' is deprecated (ADR-110 Decision 4). 'custom' requires a _note field explaining why a standard type was not feasible.

title.description: i18n translation key for the page title.

permission.description: Optional permission identifier required to access this page.

component.description: For type='custom': name resolved against the app-provided customComponents registry. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

headerComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component injected into the page's #header slot. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

actionsComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component injected into the page's #actions slot. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

sidebarComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component mounted as the default sidebar content for this page.

slots.description: Generic slot-override map. Each key is a slot name; each value is a registry component name. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed in values.

primaryAction.description: Active-page-scoped primary action rendered as an NcAppNavigationNew button above the menu list when the current route resolves to this page. Page-scoped declarations win over nav.primaryAction. Also the target of the detail page's skip link: a keyboard user tabs in, follows the link and lands on this action.

splitView.description: Index pages only. Opens a row beside the list rather than instead of it, at the sibling route <route>/split/:id that buildManifestRoutes() emits. Refused on any other page type.

board.description: Index pages only. The board view's configuration, handed to CnIndexPage as the `board` prop. The segment appears only when `viewModes` also lists `board`. Refused on any other page type.

dateAxis.description: Index pages only. The date-axis view's configuration, handed to CnIndexPage as the `dateAxis` prop. The segment appears only when `viewModes` also lists `dateAxis`. Refused on any other page type.

savedViewTree.description: Index pages only. Renders this page's saved views as a tree with labels, and declares the views that ship with the app. Refused on any other page type: a page with no saved-view dropdown has nothing to put in a tree.

manualOrder.description: Index pages only. Lets a person drag the rows into an order of their own, held per user and per list in their Nextcloud preferences and never written onto the records. Refused on any other page type.

tabInAddress.description: Detail pages only. Puts the active tab in the address as ?_tab=<id> so a link points at a tab of a record rather than at the record. The underscore prefix keeps it out of resolveQueryFilters(), which reads every other query key as a filter. Refused on any other page type.

referencePreview.description: Lets a reference on this page show a summary of the record it points at, on focus and on hover, without leaving the page. Rendered by CnReferencePreview.

widgets.description: Uniform widget placement array. Available on ALL page types in v2 (not just dashboard). Each entry specifies a widget key, slot, and grid coordinates. The cross-field constraint gridX + gridWidth <= 12 is enforced by validateManifestV2() post-schema check. Single-widget dashboards: a type:'dashboard' page with exactly one body widget covering the full 12×12 grid whose widgetKey resolves to a custom (non-library-built-in) registry component is REJECTED — see ADR-036 Decision 1 (single-widget dashboard anti-pattern). Use type:'custom' with component:'<widgetKey>' or split into N>1 widgets instead. Library built-in widget keys are exempt from the rule; the exempt set is LIBRARY_WIDGET_KEYS in src/utils/libraryWidgetKeys.js, which is held to set equality against the BUILT_IN_WIDGETS registry and the dashboard widget catalog by tests/utils/libraryWidgetKeys.spec.js. It is not restated here, because an out-of-date second copy of that list is the defect this replaced. Enforced by validateManifestV2() post-schema check.

actions.description: Typed page-level actions with a discriminator. Each action has a type field (handler | open-modal | open-page | navigate) that defaults to 'handler' when omitted.

config.description: Type-specific configuration. Shape varies by page type — see v1 schema for per-type config shapes (index, detail, dashboard, logs, settings, chat, files, form, map, custom). Config values under pages[].config may use the closed sentinel vocabulary (see $defs/sentinelTokenAny) — an out-of-vocabulary @-token FAILS validation via the sentinelGuardedValue allOf guard. Carry-forward from v1: register, schema, columns, actions, sidebar, sidebarProps, fields, sections, tabs, content, layout, widgets (dashboard only), cardComponent, columnGroups, etc.

allOf.$comment: screens-chrome-parity: a page declares ONE place to save. `saveMode` excludes a section's own `save` (flat or inside a tab) and `autosave`.

favourite.description: Deprecated and ignored: there is no star any more, a favourite is a follow with notifications off. Kept so existing manifests stay valid; use follow.

follow.description: Detail pages: the one Follow control beside the title, with a notifications on/off switch while the user follows and the follower count for a user who may update the record. Omitted means automatic: it shows when the object carries @self.watching. false removes it, and the object read then no longer asks for @self.can.

showFollowColumn.description: Index pages: add a first column with a follow toggle per row, bound to each row's @self.watching. Clicking it does not open the row. Default false.

showFavouriteColumn.description: Deprecated alias of showFollowColumn: the star column became the follow column. Default false.

personalLenses.description: Index pages: personal lenses added to the quick filters, in order. watching lists the records the user follows (labelled Following), recent the records the user opened last (it owns the order, so column sorting is off), unread the records changed since the user last looked. They combine with every other filter. favourite is a deprecated alias of watching; asking for both gives one tab. Default none.

markRead.description: Detail pages: send PUT .../read-state once after the object has rendered, when it carries @self.unread, so opening a record marks it read. Default true; false keeps the page from marking anything read.

lifecycleActions.description: Detail pages: status-gated lifecycle transition buttons (CnLifecycleActions). `inputs` gives the transition dialog hints for server-declared transitions: a map of action name to a list of { field, picker?, fields? }, merged onto the server's declared input with the same `field`. `picker` { filter, excludeSelf, labelField } narrows the records a reference input offers; `fields` names the sub-properties an object input asks for. A hint for a field the server does not declare is ignored with a console warning and never adds an input.

headerFields.description: Detail pages: fields shown as chips under the title (number, status, assignee, deadline). Each entry is a property key, or an object { key, format, labelField, colorField, warnWhenPast }. `format` is text (default), mono, badge, user or date. A `$ref` value shows `labelField` of the referenced object and falls back to the raw id in mono. An empty value shows no chip; a page without the key shows no row.
